newsitem.title: UK: Fidelity cash fund assets top $1bln, sees growth.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity cash fund assets top $1bln, sees growth.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said on Wednesday its Dublin-registered Institutional Cash Fund (ICF) had topped $1 billion under management.

It said the AAA-rated fund marketed in mark, dollar and sterling to many British institutional cash managers was expected to grow further in coming months as the cash fund concept caught on in the UK. It was launched in June 1995.
Asset under management in UK cash funds now stand at around $5 billion, against about $1 billion last year.
Peter Knight, head of institutional cash funds at Fidelity, said he expected at least a doubling of that figure in the next year.

He said factors affecting the UK market included the aftershock of the Barings collapse, the conversion of building societies to banks, regulatory changes, cost pressures, and greater accountability for custodians.

London is the largest money market centre in the world with daily turnover in the region of 50 billion sterling, although the UK's ICF market equates to less than one percent of the size of the U.S. market.
Cash funds are open-ended investment companies with variable capital. Typical charges are 15 to 20 basis points.
